name: Haleon plc

listing.exchange: London Stock Exchange (premium/ESCC); ADRs on NYSE

corporate_actions.event: FY26 organic guidance cut to ~2.5% from 3-5%; further £500m buyback

geography.fx_notes: Reports GBP; FY25 reported revenue -1.8% vs +3.0% organic (FX/divestments). Segments: North America 35%, EMEA & LatAm 42%, APAC 23%. Europe-only and UK splits not given in release. China grew mid-single digit (size not disclosed).

kpis.name: Oral Health share of revenue / organic growth

company_fcf.definition: Company FCF (net cash from operating activities less capex, plus disposals proceeds as defined by Haleon)

lease.note: GBP m, 'Payment of lease liabilities' line; lease interest not separately extracted

management.senior_turnover_5y: Tobias Hestler (CFO) replaced by Dawn Allen 2023; new Chief Growth Officer role created 2026
management.succession_notes: CEO succession not announced as of Nov-2026 (not verified)
management.guidance_record: FY25 organic 3.0% below 4-6% medium-term; FY26 3-5% guidance cut to ~2.5% in Oct-2026; profit guidance kept

ownership.controlling_holders: No controlling holder; GSK and Pfizer fully exited stakes by 2024-25 (recalled, not re-verified)

evidence: OTC/oral-care repeat consumer purchases; 6 categories, no single brand >~15% (S1)
A.rationale: Repeat consumer staples-like demand but seasonal and retail-channel exposed.

evidence: Sensodyne/parodontax +7.9% Oral Health growth, gross margin 65% (S1)
B.rationale: Leading brands with clinical claims support pricing; private label pressure in analgesics/VMS.

C.rationale: Scale in marketing/distribution but margin advantage vs peers modest.

evidence: Medium-term 4-6% but delivered 3.0% FY25 and ~2.5% FY26 (S1,S2)
EM/China and oral health penetration runway (S1)
D.rationale: Moderate runway; recent delivery below target.

E.rationale: Well spread; no country >40% (US is largest, below 35%).

evidence: Physical OTC products; AI search could alter brand discovery
AI cameras in Suzhou plant cited (S1)
Cold/flu season and US consumer drove misses (S2)
Adjusted vs reported op profit gap small (£2,526m vs £2,412m) (S1)

sector_specific.patent_exposure_pct: <5% (INFERENCE: OTC brands rely on trademarks/claims; Rx-to-OTC exclusivities not material)
sector_specific.top_product_pct: Oral Health category 32%; largest brand (Sensodyne) share not disclosed in release
sector_specific.litigation: Legacy Zantac (ranitidine) claims: Haleon stated in 2022 it would not indemnify GSK/Pfizer and is not party to material claims (recalled, not re-verified); no provision noted in FY25 release

gates.notes: G1 2.6x <3.5x. G3 no patent cliff. G6 none. Zantac legacy tracked as tail risk.

bull_points: Oral Health (32% of sales) compounding high-single-digit with clinical brands
Strong FCF (£1.9bn) funds steady buybacks at ~2.5x leverage
bear_points: Organic growth has decelerated from 9% (2022) to ~2.5% (2026 guide), below 4-6% target
US consumer/retailer destocking and private-label substitution in pain/VMS/respiratory
Dependence on price (+2.3%) with weak volume (+0.7%)
thesis_breakers: Net debt/EBITDA rises above 3.0x without M&A rationale
Oral Health organic growth falls below 4% for two consecutive halves
